apod.explanation: Using NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what triggers repeated outbursts from the giant, unstable star AT 2016blu in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, about 30 million light-years away. The star, at least 33 times the Sun's mass, brightens and dims every 113 days as a previously hidden companion — a black hole or a neutron star — pulls material from it, heating the gas until it shines brightly in X-rays. The composite image, released Nov. 9, 2026, shows the galaxy tilted at a sharp angle, with the outbursting star marked near its outer edge.
apod.title: Outbursts from a Massive Star

breaking.fact: President Trump threatened Thursday to immediately double U.S. tariffs on Mexican goods — from 10% to 20% on most goods — unless Mexico stops migrant caravans heading north; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he is still optimistic the U.S. can reach trade deals with Mexico and Canada, a day after the threat landed amid sensitive USMCA renegotiations.
breaking.headline: Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs

breaking.fact: A global Microsoft 365 outage that began Thursday afternoon knocked out Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Copilot for users in 74 countries, with Downdetector logging more than 130,000 U.S. Outlook reports at the peak; Microsoft says servers failed automated health checks and overloaded the rest, with no sign of a cyberattack, and recovery was progressing Friday with shares down about 3% in premarket trading.
breaking.headline: Microsoft 365 outage stretches into a second day

breaking.fact: U.S. existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to a 3.75 million annual rate, the lowest since August 2010 and 8.8% below a year earlier, as the average 30-year mortgage hit 7.33% — its highest since 2000 — even as inventory rose 1.3% to 1.59 million homes.
breaking.headline: Existing-home sales fall to a 16-year low

breaking.fact: Spot gold traded near $3,895 Friday morning, down about 4% for the week, as hot CPI and PPI readings pushed the 10-year Treasury yield above 5.1% and hardened expectations of a December Fed rate hike.
breaking.headline: Gold slides about 4% on the week as yields top 5.1%

items.body: Reuters reports the IRGC navy said Friday that a tanker carrying liquefied natural gas struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz and suffered an explosion while using what Tehran called an “unauthorised and dangerous route”; Iranian media reported Thursday that four oil tankers were hit by explosions after entering waters Iran considers restricted. On oil, Kpler's tracking shows Iranian crude loadings have been zero since late August — the first zero month since Kpler began tracking in 2013 — while non-Iranian crude is still moving, with Kpler putting direct Hormuz crude exports at about 7.3 million barrels a day in the week to October 28.
items.headline: Latest from the Strait

space.body: SpaceX released the flight plan today for Starship Flight 15, still targeting a 4:45–6:40 PM CT window Friday evening from Starbase, but the FAA launch license had still not been issued as of Friday morning — the last hurdle before the first attempt to catch both stages. Booster 22 and Ship 42, both Block 3 vehicles, would fly the first double catch, with Ship 42 deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and a ship catch possible around 2:45 PM CT Saturday; the same window is available Saturday as backup.
space.headline: SpaceX releases Starship Flight 15 flight plan as license clock ticks down

space.body: Gladstone Institutes researchers found the blood-brain barrier is a selective filter that picks helpful proteins from the blood and delivers them to the right brain cells — 92 of 861 tagged blood proteins crossed in mice. The liver protein apolipoprotein A1, which helps maintain connections between neurons, was among them; in Alzheimer's-model mice, restoring its supply eased early signs of the disease. The work was published in Cell.
space.headline: Blood-brain barrier is a filter, not a wall — a new Alzheimer's lead

space.body: Astronomers using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile have discovered two previously hidden companions of the Milky Way — the ultra-faint galaxy Aquarius 4 in the galaxy's distant outskirts and a star cluster, Rubin GC1, on the far side — adding to the roughly 65 known satellite galaxies orbiting our own. The findings were reported in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.
space.headline: Rubin Observatory finds two hidden neighbours of the Milky Way

space.body: A Gachon University team has developed a multifunctional nanozyme that breaks down biofilms — the protective layers bacteria form on surfaces — by simultaneously attacking their DNA, protein and polysaccharide components. In tests it removed biofilms formed by E. coli and Staphylococcus aureus, kept more than 80% of its activity after 60 uses, and held up after 100 days in storage. The study was published in Advanced Functional Materials.
space.headline: Nanozyme that dissolves bacterial biofilms could fight drug-resistant infections

weekInBrief.body: Nvidia shares are down about 14% this week after founder-CEO Jensen Huang resigned Nov 11; interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first test when the company reports earnings Tuesday, Nov 17.

weekInBrief.body: The U.S. dollar index held above 103, its highest since April 2025, after three days of gains on persistent-inflation fears, while the yen traded near 160 per dollar — the level markets watch for Japanese intervention — and Japan's finance minister renewed warnings against speculative moves.
weekInBrief.headline: Dollar hits a 19-month high as yen nears 160

weekInBrief.body: Traders now put an 88% chance on a quarter-point Fed hike in December, with a 12% chance of a half-point move, after hot CPI and PPI readings; Fed Governor Michelle Bowman said Thursday “there is still work to do” to bring inflation back to 2%.
weekInBrief.headline: Markets price an 88% chance of a December Fed hike
